To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the (R)-enantiomer of the chiral attractant DHMA binds to the periplasmically located serine-binding pocket of the Tsr chemoreceptor of Escherichium coli with higher affinity than the (S)-enantiomer and promotes a stronger attractant chemotactic response than the (S) enatiomer.

(R)-3,4-dimethylmandelic acid is a stronger chemoattractant for Escherichia coli than (S)-3,4-Dimethylmandelic Acid because of the stronger piston-like pushdown on α4 helix upon binding to the Tsr chemoreceptor.

we used a combination of state-of-the-art molecular docking and simulation tools to computationally predict that the (R)-enantiomer of 3,4- dihydroxymandelic (DHMA) acid is a stronger chemoattractant than the (S)-enantiomer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism by which a ligand, DHMA, is recognized by the Tsr chemoreceptor.
the molecular mechanism by which a ligand is sensed by a receptor and how that information is transmitted to the cytoplasmic signaling domain.
the molecular mechanisms of chemoreceptor-mediated bacterial motility, and it has the potential to lead to new strategies for controlling bacterial behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(R)-3,4-dydroxymandelate (DHMA) is the active ligand for Tsr, and (S)-3,4-DHMA has no effect on chemotaxis, but this conclusion would be based on the assumption that the ligand is not degraded by the cells, which is unlikely to be true.

(R)-3,4-dydroxymandelate (R-DHMA), but not (S)-3,4- dihydroxymandelate, (S)-DHM, is a chemoattractant for E. coli, and that the difference in chemoattraction is due to the difference in the magnitude of the piston-like motion of the α-helices of the pTserine receptor.
the (R)-enantiomer of DHMA, but not the (S)-enantiomer, is a chemoattractant for E. coli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
(R)-3,4-dhydroxymandelic acid is a better attractant than (R)-3-hydroxymandelate, and that (R)- and (S)-3,4-Dhydroxymandelate are better attractants than (R)- and (S)-3-Hydroxymandelates.
we computationally and experimentally showed that DHMA, a chemoattractant, is a racemic mixture and that (R)-isomer of DHMA is the active chemoattracting species.
the (R)-DH MA is the more effective chemoattractant than (S) DHMA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the (S)-DHMAs are less effective than their (R)-enantiomers at inducing chemotaxis.
it is possible to computationally predict and experimentally validate the molecular basis of the chemoreceptor response to chiral ligands, even when the ligand is generated within the cell.
the chiral specificity of the chemotactic response to DHMA is determined by the chirality of the ligand, not by the chirality at the ligand binding site.
